questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — internal-case-management-system (case management, Next.js + Prisma). Verified finding A3: the `case:assign` permission is never checked. `CASE_WORKER` does not hold it, yet `createCase()` and `updateCase()` accept `assignedToId` after checking only `case:create` / `case:update`, so a case worker can assign any user on their team. You will delegate the fix to a coding agent. Write the brief: goal, allowed files, boundaries, test command, stop condition. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal: any create or update request that sets `assignedToId` is refused with 403 unless the actor holds `case:assign`; both `createCase()` and `updateCase()` enforce it.
[w3] The new check fires only when an assignee is supplied: a CASE_WORKER must still be able to create and edit unassigned cases, because the role keeps `case:create` and `case:update`.
[w2] Reuse `ensurePermission(actor, "case:assign")` from authorize.ts instead of an inline role-name `if`, so the rule stays in the central permission map.
[w2] Allowed files: src/services/caseService.ts and tests next to it (vitest only includes src/**/*.test.ts and src/**/*.test.tsx).

[w3] Boundary: the permission matrix in permissions.ts is not edited (no granting `case:assign` to CASE_WORKER, no deleting it), and the team-move finding A4 and `escalation:manage` stay out of scope.
keyPoints.quote: The matrix promises something the services never enforce.

keyPoints.text: [w2] Test command: `npm test` (vitest run) plus `npm run typecheck`, with the repositories and db mocked through vi.mock as the existing caseService test already does for listCases.

[w2] Stop condition: tests show a CASE_WORKER with an assignee gets AuthorizationError on create and on update, a TEAM_LEAD with an assignee succeeds, and a CASE_WORKER without one succeeds; UI changes are reported, not made.

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. What are the likeliest ways an agent goes wrong on this task, and what in your brief prevents each?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It calls `ensurePermission(actor, "case:assign")` unconditionally at the top of createCase, so case workers can no longer open any case at all.
[w3] It guards only the create path, or only hides the Assignee select in the form, while the PATCH path still connects `assignedToId` unchecked.
[w2] It 'resolves' the dead permission by changing policy: granting `case:assign` to CASE_WORKER or removing the permission from the matrix.
[w2] It places the check inside `db.$transaction` after the record write, the ordering mistake this file's own header warns about.
[w1] It also starts fixing team moves, the separate A4 problem, growing the diff beyond the brief.
keyPoints.quote: so the old assignee stays attached to a case owned by a different team

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent says assignment is now enforced and tests pass. What do you check before you accept it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] The new CASE_WORKER-with-assignee tests are red on the original service (the assignment goes through) and green on the fix; ask for both runs.
[w3] The negative controls are present: a CASE_WORKER without an assignee and a TEAM_LEAD with one both still succeed.
[w2] permissions.ts and the Prisma schema are untouched in the diff.
[w2] The refusal surfaces as a 403 because it throws AuthorizationError, which the route error handler maps by status, not as a generic 500.
[w1] The handback flags the UI follow-up: the create form still shows the Assignee select to case workers, who will now get a 403 if they use it.
